summary: Researched the roadmap preflight approval gate: detect_layout is safely extractable into a new shared library (roadmap-integration.sh parses argv at top level with no run-guard, so sourcing the whole file is unsafe); the gate fires only on absent/unknown verdicts; the real skill-roadmap write call lives in roadmap-agent.md's Write Contract, so the interactive gate belongs in skill-roadmap Stage 1 pre-dispatch, modeled on skill-meta Section 2; the conclusion stage's Bash allow-list needs two new entries and issue-record.sh's per-task scoping tension is resolved via Move 5's existing events-append.sh pattern; no seed issue-log class fits precisely, so a new class is recommended.

artifacts.summary: Full research findings: library extraction design, 4-way verdict classification, interactive-arm placement in skill-roadmap Stage 1, non-interactive-arm design for conclusion stage Step 5, new issue-log class recommendation, and scaffold placeholder content design.

next_steps: Run /orchestrate 625 to create an implementation plan from these findings.

memory_candidates.content: roadmap-integration.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/) parses $@ and calls exit at its own top level, outside any function and with no BASH_SOURCE run-guard. A caller that needs its detect_layout classification logic must extract the relevant functions into a sourced library (the status-vocabulary.sh 'one sourced shared library, many consumers' shape) rather than sourcing the whole script, which would re-execute its argument parser and could exit the sourcing shell.

AskUserQuestion is measured categorically withheld from every Agent-tool dispatch of a named subagent_type (agent-frontmatter-standard.md), independent of tools:/disallowedTools: config. Any skill needing a user-choice point before dispatching a subagent must collect it in the skill's own pre-dispatch stage. skill-meta/SKILL.md Section 2 is the proven reference template for this shape: ask, hold the resolved answer, pass it into the delegation context, dispatch only after.

issue-record.sh is fundamentally per-task (--task-dir/--task N, directory must exist). /orchestrate's conclusion stage (Move 5) is explicitly NOT task-scoped per-se at the batch level; its own channels (b)/(c) already route non-task-scoped evidence to events-append.sh -> specs/events.jsonl for exactly that reason, even though Move 5 does carry a resolved per-task list it can loop over when a per-task issues.jsonl entry is also wanted. Any future non-task-scoped caller needing to use issue-record.sh should follow this dual-write precedent rather than inventing a non-task-scoped exception to that script's contract.
